 Iran grain trade shrugs off US blockade as Hormuz bulker traffic stays resilient
 Iran-linked bulker traffic through Hormuz remains above pre-blockade levels, with October arrivals already pointing to sustained grain import demand
 Latin America accounts for 74% of Iran’s seaborne agricultural imports, and analysts say US blockade has done little to alter established trade flows from Brazil and Argentina
 Greek-owned and -operated bulkers account for nearly half of Iran-linked transits, highlighting shipowners’ willingness to accept elevated geopolitical risk
 13 Oct 2026 
 Analysis
 Ece Göksedef 
 @ecegoksedef 
 [email protected] 
 Iran’s grain imports continue to flow through the Strait of Hormuz despite the US naval blockade, with Brazilian cargoes and Greek-operated bulkers underpinning trade volumes that remain above pre-MOU levels
